div.head: [Inclosure 1.—Translation.]
div.p: We hereby sanction the law relating to the judicature in Korea which was approved by the Diet and cause the same to be promulgated.
div.closer:
June 25, 1906.
(Countersigned) Marquis Kimmochi Saionji, Prime Minister,
Masahira Matsuda, Minister of Justice.

p.hi: law relating to the judicature in korea.

list.label: I.
list.item: The residency shall conduct the preliminary examinations of lawsuits and perform duties connected with noncontentious procedure within its jurisdiction.
list.label: II.
list.item: The resident-general may transfer the judicial business of one residency to another.
list.label: III.
list.item: In the residency the resident or the vice-resident alone shall examine and pronounce judgment.
list.label: IV.
list.item: The court of the residency-general shall examine appeals concerning decisions of the residents and give final judgment.
list.label: V.
list.item: The court of the residency-general shall be composed of three judges, of whom the highest in rank shall be presiding judge.
list.label: VI.
list.item: Only those who have been judges, prosecuting attorneys, professors of law in the Imperial University, residents, vice-residents, or attorneys at law for at least five years may be judges or prosecuting attorneys of the court of the residency-general.
list.label: VII.
list.item: The resident shall cause the officials of the residency to act as prosecuting attorneys of the residency.
list.label: VIII.
list.item: The prosecuting business of the court of the residency-general shall be dealt with by the prosecuting attorney.
list.label: IX.
list.item: The provisions for legal cooperation in the judiciary law for courts and the Formosan court shall be applied respectively to the legal cooperation between the residencies and the residency-general court on the one hand, and the court on the other, and between the residencies and the residency-general court on the one hand, and the Formosan court on the other. The provisions for legal cooperation by request of foreign law courts shall be applied to legal assistance to be rendered in the residencies and the residency-general.
list.label: X.
list.item: Concerning the laws to be applied to Korea with respect to judicial matters not provided for in this law, Imperial ordinances may be issued.

postscript.p: The date at which this law is to be put into force shall be determined by an Imperial ordinance.
The lawsuits and noncontentious cases filed prior to the date at which this law is put into force shall be dealt with as formerly.
We hereby sanction the ordinance relating to the date at which law No. 56 will be put into force, and cause the same to be promulgated.
postscript.closer:
June 25, 1906.
(Countersigned) Marquis Kimmochi Saionji,
Prime Minister.

postscript.p: Law No. 56 of 1906 shall be put into force on the 27th of June, 1906.
